Two design details changed under measurement of the 86-record corpus: a work item's git-copied message is not scanned for mentions, because a relation derived from it could never be corrected, and prose that shows the target grammar must use placeholders, because a well-formed target in prose is a citation -- the ticket's own Body was failing that rule against itself. Body.raw:
Add a NOTES section to a todo record: facts and findings as first-class,
status-free nodes, so `Body` can be pure implementation strategy. Notes are
addressable by objid, so a fact written once can be referenced from another
todo instead of retold.

Scope: a top-level `Notes` list; a `relto` relation list on the three
prose-bearing node kinds; a `note-*` / `relto-*` command family; doctor
maintenance of the one auto-derived relation type; note rendering in the web
viewer; and the skill-doc rewrite that makes agents actually use the split.

## The node shapes

`Notes` is an optional top-level list. A note node holds exactly:

    {"objid": "0012", "raw": "<the fact or finding>", "relto": [...]}

No `kind`, no `done`, no status of any sort. A note is a fact, and a fact has
no disposition to record; that absence is the point. Anything that needs a
status is a WorkItem, and anything that needs a branch is a subtodo.

A `relto` element holds exactly:

    {"objid": "0013", "type": "<relation type>", "target": "<qualified target>"}

`relto` lives on THREE node kinds and nowhere else: `Body`, every `Notes`
element, every `WorkItems` element. Absent means no relations; an empty list is
equivalent and is not written. `Summary`, `LongSummary`, `AC` and `Tag` do not
get one.

## The target grammar

A `target` is ALWAYS namespace-qualified -- there is no bare spelling, in the
store or in prose. Three forms, and only these:

    objid:<hex>                 an object in THIS record
    todo:<hex>                  a whole todo
    todo:<hex>/objid:<hex>      an object in another todo's record

Prose that SHOWS the grammar writes the placeholder spelling above. A
well-formed target in prose is a CITATION, and doctor derives a mention from
it, so an illustrative example spelled as a real target would derive a
relation to an object that was never meant to exist.

Every hex component takes 4+ characters, the permalink floor rather than the
CLI's zero-padding shortcut: a target is matched against every object in a
record, where a shorter prefix is a coin flip rather than an abbreviation.

A target is stored AS WRITTEN and resolved at use time, exactly like every
other selector the tool takes. A prefix that later becomes ambiguous is a
doctor finding, not a silent mismatch.

An `objid:` target may name ANY object in a record, not only a note -- a
WorkItem, a `Subtodos` entry, `Body`, another relto element. Validation is
therefore "this objid exists in that record" and nothing narrower.

**A `todo:` target creates no obligation of any kind.** No merge obligation, no
INFO back-link, no wait edge. `add-subtodo` and `set --parent` remain the only
ways to make a structural todo-to-todo link; relto is a reader's cross-
reference and nothing more.

One grammar serves three places: the value stored in `target`, the token doctor
scans prose for, and the way the house id convention already writes ids in
prose. Do not introduce a second spelling for any of them.

## Relation types

`mention` is DERIVED and owned by doctor. Every other type is manual, and
doctor never touches a non-`mention` entry: not its target, not its type, not
its position. That single rule is what makes an auto-maintained field safe to
hand-edit, and it holds identically on `Body`, on notes, and on work items.

Seeded vocabulary: `mention` (auto) and `relates` (the manual default).
Extending it is an allow-list entry; an unknown type is an error, never a
silent pass-through.

## Doctor's mention sync

Doctor scans a relto-bearing node's EDITABLE prose -- `raw` and `summary`,
named once in one constant, not discovered by walking strings -- for target
tokens, and reconciles that node's `mention` entries to exactly what its text
says: add one for a target the text gained, drop one for a target the text
lost, leave every other type alone. A target already carried by a manual entry
is already related, so no second `mention` is derived for it.

A work item's `message` is NOT scanned. It is copied from git when the item is
completed and is not editable afterwards, so a relation derived from it could
never be corrected.

**Idempotence is a hard requirement.** A second consecutive doctor run over an
unchanged record allocates no objid, changes no byte, bumps no `update_dt`, and
makes no commit. Doctor runs constantly and commits what it repairs, so a sync
that churned `_nextobjid` every pass would bury the store's real history. Patch
entries in place; never delete-and-recreate one that is still wanted.

Unresolvable targets are findings, not hard failures: a dangling LOCAL target
is a finding, and an unresolvable CROSS-TODO target is a soft warning only,
because the store is per-repo and a target naming a todo in another repo's
store is legitimately unresolvable here. Malformed relto SHAPE stays a hard
fail like every other node-shape check.

## What `prompt` emits

`build_prompt_chain` (todo.py:2559) gains notes, under two hard limits:

1. **Notes only.** A `Body.relto` target naming a WorkItem, a subtodo, or
   anything else is legal and is NOT emitted. `prompt` has never propagated
   `AC` or `WorkItems`, and a relto target is not a way around that.
2. **This record only.** A `todo:` or `todo:.../objid:` target is NOT chased.
   It is emitted as a one-line pointer naming the target, so an agent learns
   the fact exists and can read it deliberately, and no prompt ever inlines a
   foreign record's text.

Within one record the walk IS transitive: `Body.relto` -> notes -> those notes'
own `relto` -> further notes. Cycles are therefore reachable, and are handled
the way the parent walk already handles them -- one `seen` set, membership
checked before descent, a node reached twice emitted once. Reuse that
discipline rather than inventing a depth cap.

Each note is emitted after its record's `Body`, under a header carrying its
objid, so an agent can cite the fact it used.

## Display

Notes render between `Body` and `Work items`, REUSING the work-item display
machinery rather than growing a parallel one: `_box_attrs`, `_objid_badge`,
`_clamped`, `_section`, the `.row` / `.wi` CSS family, the objid-keyed fold
objects map, and the `hi` cross-highlight list (todo_web.py:376, 395, 563, 815).

Do not add a note branch inside `_wi_box` (todo_web.py:395). A note has no
checkbox, no `sha` chip and no `todo:` chip, so a shared box function becomes a
status/no-status switch; a sibling `_note_box` calling the same primitives keeps
both readable.

Locally-resolved relto targets are exactly what the existing `hi` mechanism
already does: clicking a note highlights the work item it bears on, for free.

`Notes` must join `_DEDICATED_FIELDS` (todo_web.py:544), or `_meta_html` dumps
the raw dicts, and `_focusable_objids` (todo_web.py:1354), or a permalink to a
note focuses nothing.

No permalink GRAMMAR change is needed. `todo_url`'s drop-the-s alias already
makes `/<todoid>/note/0/raw` resolve, and `/<todoid>/objid/<hex>` already finds
an object anywhere in a record.

## Storage and migration

`Notes` and `relto` are optional and absent-means-none, exactly like
`LongSummary`, `ActualSummary` and `Tag`. No record migration and no
`todo_db.SCHEMA_VERSION` bump: there is nothing in an existing record to
rewrite, and a v10 that only adds an absent field is a no-op sweep over the
whole store.

## The doc rewrite is part of the feature

Notes exist so that a `Body` is pure strategy, and that only happens if the
skill says so. `BODY.md` is the normative owner of what-goes-where and changes
materially: facts and findings move out of the `Body` into notes, and its
propagation table stops reading "Summary and Body. Nothing else."

Every doc asserting the old propagation contract becomes false the moment
`prompt` changes; `grep -rn "Nothing else" *.md` finds the load-bearing one.

## Out of scope, deliberately

No search or embedding work on note text. Note `raw` does NOT join
`_EMBED_FIELDS` / `_iter_embed_targets` (todo.py:438, 519) here, and no
note-specific query syntax is added. Notes are write, display and reference
only in this ticket; making them searchable is a follow-on todo.

LongSummary.raw:
Todo records currently commingle implementation strategy with the facts and findings discovered while working, all inside one `Body` string. This adds a `Notes` list to the record -- status-free nodes holding one fact each, `{objid, raw, relto}` -- so the `Body` can shrink to pure strategy and a fact can be referenced instead of retold. Because every nested object already carries an immutable `objid`, a note is permanently addressable, and one todo's note can be cited from another.

Cross-references are carried by a `relto` list that lives on `Body`, on every note, and on every work item. A relto element is `{objid, type, target}`, where `target` is always namespace-qualified: `objid:0034` for an object in the same record, `todo:dea7` for a whole todo, `todo:c03d/objid:0045` for an object in another todo. An `objid:` target may name any object in a record, not only a note. A `todo:` target is a reader's cross-reference only -- it creates no merge obligation and no INFO back-link, which remain the business of `add-subtodo` and `set --parent`.

One relation type, `mention`, is derived: `todo.py doctor` scans each relto-bearing node's prose (`raw`, `summary`, `message`) for target tokens and reconciles that node's `mention` entries to what the text actually says, while never touching an entry of any other type. Doctor's sync must be idempotent to the byte -- no objid churn, no `update_dt` bump, no commit on an unchanged record -- because doctor runs constantly and commits its own repairs.

`todo.py prompt` starts emitting notes, which is what makes the strategy/facts split safe: a fresh agent still gets Summary plus Body for every ancestor, and now also the notes reachable through that record's `Body.relto`, transitively, cycle-safe via the same `seen` set the parent walk uses. It emits notes only -- never a work item, never a subtodo -- and it does not chase a `todo:` target into another record, emitting a one-line pointer instead.

The web viewer gains a `Notes` section between `Body` and `Work items`, built from the existing work-item box primitives (`_box_attrs`, `_objid_badge`, `_clamped`, `_section`, the fold objects map and its `hi` cross-highlight list) rather than a parallel renderer, and with no status affordance on a note box. No permalink grammar change is needed: `/<todoid>/note/0/raw` already resolves through `todo_url`'s drop-the-s alias, and `/<todoid>/objid/<hex>` already finds an object anywhere in a record. `Notes` and `relto` are optional and absent-means-none, so no record migration and no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump.

The skill documentation is part of the deliverable, not a follow-up: `BODY.md` is rewritten so `Body` is pure strategy with facts in notes, and its propagation table -- today "Summary and Body. Nothing else." -- becomes false the moment `prompt` changes. Search is deliberately out of scope: note text does not join the embedding or IDF target list in this ticket.

Notes.raw: IMPLEMENTATION.md carries the relto row inside the top-level field table (the one holding Summary, Body, AC, ActualSummary, Tag, Notes), where every other row is a top-level field. relto is nested: it lives on Body, on a Notes element and on a WorkItems element, and ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS does not include it. Notes and relto want a section of their own, describing the node shapes, the target grammar and the host spellings in one place.

A target already carried by a MANUAL relto entry is already related, so doctor's mention sync does not add a second entry of type mention for it. Reconciliation is: for every target the prose names, ensure SOME entry exists on that node (a manual entry counts); remove only mention entries whose target the prose no longer names. This is what keeps the one-host-relates-to-one-target-once rule that relto-add already enforces by refusing a duplicate target.

Prose that SHOWS the target grammar writes the placeholder spelling (objid:<hex>, todo:<hex>, todo:<hex>/objid:<hex>). A well-formed target in prose is a CITATION and doctor derives a mention from it, so an illustrative example spelled out as a real target derives a relation to an object that was never meant to exist. This ticket's own Body hit exactly that: its grammar table spelled each example as a real four-hex target and so stood as a permanent dangling-target finding. The rule belongs in the guidance objid:000d rewrites.

A note reaches a fresh agent only through Body.relto, which objid:000a implements. A note relto'd to a WORK ITEM does not travel: the worker reads work-item-read, which prints the item alone, and prompt emits work-item relations not at all. So a hazard recorded against one step is invisible to the agent working that step. The obvious completion is for work-item-read to print the notes its own relto reaches, alongside the item. Out of scope for this ticket as planned; it needs the user's call before anyone adds it.

WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] prompt emits notes. WorkItems.message:
web viewer: a Notes section between Body and Work items

Notes render as boxes built from the work-item box primitives -- _box_attrs,
_objid_badge, _clamped, _section, the .wi CSS family, the objid-keyed fold map
-- so a note tile behaves like every other tile: click it for the full text,
its objid is a permalink, an oversized list collapses with an N-notes hint.
_note_box is a sibling of _wi_box rather than a branch inside it, because a
note has no checkbox, no sha chip and no todo chip, and a shared box would
become a status/no-status switch. A test asserts those absences directly.

relto renders as chips under the Body text and on note and work-item boxes,
each showing its relation type so a derived mention reads differently from a
manual relates. A chip linking rule, not a guess: a local target that resolves
anchors to /<todoid>/objid/<objid>, a todo: target links to that todo's page,
a dangling one renders as plain text rather than a dead link, and the static
read-only repr never grows a link at all.

A note's fold entry sets hi to the objids its relto resolves to locally, so
clicking a note highlights the work item it bears on -- the existing
cross-highlight mechanism, no new machinery.

Notes joins _DEDICATED_FIELDS, or _meta_html dumps the raw dicts, and
_focusable_objids, or a permalink to a note focuses nothing. A record without
Notes renders exactly as before; the section is absent rather than empty,
matching Long summary.

The permalink grammar needed no change: todo_url's drop-the-s alias already
routes /<todoid>/note/0/raw to Notes.

WorkItems.message:
BODY.md: facts and findings are Notes; the Body is pure strategy

The doctrine file now says where a FACT goes, which is the whole point of
notes: the Body carries what to DO, a note carries what was FOUND. A table
splits Body / Note / WorkItem / subtodo by that test, and the tie-breaker is
status -- anything needing done, blocked or obsolete is a WorkItem, because a
note has none by construction.

The propagation rule is rewritten around what actually travels. It read
'Summary and Body. Nothing else.'; it now reads Summary, Body, and the notes
the Body cites, with the table gaining a row for a cited note and the
WorkItems row saying that a note cited only from a work item does not travel
either. Body.relto is named as the switch that publishes a fact to every
descendant.

Two rules that cost something to learn are stated outright: doctor owns the
mention type, so writing objid:<hex> into a Body sentence IS citing it and the
relation appears unasked; and prose that SHOWS the grammar writes placeholders,
since a well-formed target in prose is a citation and an illustrative example
spelled as a real target leaves a dangling-target finding nobody can explain.

The never-mirror-the-WorkItems-list rule extends to notes: relto and the
rendered Notes section already say which note bears on what.

Every command and file this doc cites was resolved against the tree.
WorkItems.summary: [HICAP] Rewrite BODY.md. Body becomes PURE STRATEGY: facts, findings, inventories and measurements move to notes. Add notes to the what-goes-where doctrine as a fourth home alongside Body / WorkItem / subtodo, with the test for each. Rewrite the propagation section: the table asserting prompt emits Summary and Body and 'Nothing else.' is false once notes travel, and the new rule (notes reachable through Body.relto travel; AC and WorkItems still do not) is what the whole layout now rests on. Keep the existing prohibition on mirroring the WorkItems list, and extend the same reasoning to notes: a Body must not enumerate its notes, because relto and the rendered Notes section already do.

Two ambiguities this feature created, fixed here: 'Durable notes belong in the
commit message' now distinguishes durable COMMENTARY from a durable FACT, and
the handoff report asks for note gists rather than a count.
